source: Thérèse de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), Knitting chapter.
publicDomainStatus: Public domain. Published 1886, well past US / UK / EU copyright terms.
creditPattern: Fig. {NNN}, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (Thérèse de Dillmont, 1886). Public domain.
batchNotes: K-4.2 batch totals 20 figures across two rounds. Round 1 (pause batch): 10 figures covering position-of-hands, 3 cast-on variants, knit, purl, k tbl, yarn-over, sock heel, plaited stitch. Round 2 (extension): 10 more covering remaining Dillmont cast-on variants, purl tbl, knot stitch (bobble ancestor), brioche x 2, two-colour colorwork, drop-stitch lace. Filename convention: fig-{figureNumber}-{slug}.jpg. The Project Gutenberg image filenames (352.jpg, 353.jpg, ...) are sequential and do NOT match figure numbers; the cross-reference is in each entry's sourceFile.

fig-341-position-of-the-hands.jpg.caption: Position of the hands in knitting (English / French style)

fig-342-crossed-casting-on-single-thread.caption: Crossed casting on with a single thread (Dillmont's name; the modern long-tail cast-on)

fig-345-knitting-on-stitches.jpg.caption: Knitting on stitches (the modern knitted-on cast-on)

fig-348-casting-on-with-picots.jpg.caption: Casting on with picots (decorative cast-on for lace edges)

fig-349-plain-stitch-knit.jpg.caption: Plain stitch (Dillmont's name; the modern knit stitch)

fig-350-back-or-seam-stitch-purl.jpg.caption: Back or seam-stitch (Dillmont's name; the modern purl stitch)

fig-351-plain-stitch-taken-from-behind.j.caption: Plain stitch taken from behind (the modern knit through back loop, k tbl)

fig-382-plaited-stitch.jpg.caption: Plaited stitch (the Victorian forerunner of modern cabling)

fig-343-double-crossed-casting-on.jpg.caption: Double crossed casting on (a denser variant of the long-tail cast-on)

fig-344-crossed-casting-on-forming-a-cha.caption: Crossed casting on, forming a chain (a chain-edge cast-on variant)

fig-346-casting-on-with-slip-loops.jpg.caption: Casting on with slip loops (the Continental / German cast-on family)

fig-347-casting-on-with-double-slip-loop.caption: Casting on with double slip loops (a stretchier slip-loop variant for open patterns)

fig-352-back-stitch-from-behind-purl-tbl.caption: Back or seam-stitch taken from behind (the modern purl through back loop, p tbl)

fig-354-knot-stitch.jpg.caption: Knot stitch (the Victorian forerunner of the modern bobble / popcorn)

fig-380-plain-patent-brioche.jpg.caption: Plain patent knitting, or brioche pattern (the foundational brioche stitch)

fig-381-double-patent-brioche.jpg.caption: Double patent knitting (the two-colour brioche variant)

fig-386-two-colour-stranded-colorwork.jp.caption: Knitting pattern with two threads (Victorian stranded two-colour colorwork, the Fair Isle / Selbu ancestor)

fig-387-dropped-stitch-pattern.jpg.caption: Knitting pattern with dropped stitches (a Victorian drop-stitch lace technique)

covered: Cast-on (7 Dillmont variants): crossed / long-tail (single, double, chain), knitted-on, picot, slip-loop, double slip-loop
Knit through back loop (plain stitch from behind)
Purl through back loop (back stitch from behind)
Two-colour stranded colorwork (Fair Isle / Selbu ancestor)

notCovered.bind-off-illustration: Dillmont's 'Casting off' section is text-only; no figure. Will need to source from Weldon's or in-house illustration.
notCovered.modern-named-decreases: ssk, k2tog, cdd are not separately illustrated. Dillmont describes 'intakes' (decreases) inline within stocking instructions.
notCovered.modern-named-increases: M1, kfb, lifted increase. Dillmont names 'over' (yarn-over) but not the other modern increases.
notCovered.cable-cross-front-back: Plaited stitch (fig. 382) is the closest. Modern c4f / c4b would need Weldon's or in-house.
notCovered.backward-loop-cast-on: Not covered (similar to slip-loop casts but not separately illustrated).
notCovered.picking-up-stitches: Mentioned in stocking instructions but no dedicated figure.
notCovered.magic-loop-dpn-two-circulars: Modern techniques (post-WW2). Will need in-house parametric schematic.

nextSourcesToTry: Weldon's Practical Knitter volumes (1880s-1900s) on Internet Archive for bind-off + more cast-on coverage
Beeton's Book of Needlework (1870) for additional Victorian coverage
